group: q|what shoe size is top 1% for men in the united states

result.why: No national statistics office, peer-reviewed study or data-holding organisation publishes a percentile distribution of shoe size for US men. Healthline states there is no official data on US men's shoe sizes, and the search results that do give numbers are retail blogs and SEO pages with no stated sample or method. The nearest measured proxy is foot length, but I could not get a usable credible percentile for it either. (1) Jurca, Zabkar and Dzeroski 2019 (Scientific Reports, PMC6914786) analysed Volumental 3D scans of 494,833 North American men. It reports only the modal length class (270 mm) plus width, instep and heel percentiles within that class, with no foot-length percentiles. The 2018 preliminary paper (3DBODY.TECH, doi 10.15221/18.281) shows only a kernel density plot. (2) ANSUR II (2012 US Army survey, 4,082 men, Gordon et al. 2014, NATICK/TR-15/007) does publish measured foot-length percentiles up to the 99th, but the report and the public CSV could not be retrieved in this session (DTIC returned 403, and the Penn State mirror failed with a certificate error). It is also a military sample, not the general population. (3) The FAA Technical Operations survey appendix (Bradtmiller et al. 2008) does not include foot length. Converting a foot-length percentile to a US shoe size would also need a sizing-chart conversion, which is my own computation and not a published value. Suggested follow-up: add a 'foot_length_mm' measure sourced from the ANSUR II summary report (p50 and p99 for men, once retrieved) and present shoe size only as an approximate label, with the caveat that ANSUR II is a measured Army sample.
